articles.title: Rohit Sharma's 30 Runs in New Zealand Put World Cup Place in Doubt
articles.excerpt: The former captain averaged 7.50 across four innings in the 3-1 series win, and Kapil Dev has left his future to the selectors ahead of the Sri Lanka series.
articles.image_caption: Rohit Sharma bats in the nets during an India training session. The former captain scored 30 runs in four innings in the New Zealand ODI series, putting his place in India's 2027 World Cup plans under scrutiny.
articles.nri_angle: Rohit's World Cup future is the selection debate diaspora fans will follow through the Sri Lanka home series in December and into the 2027 tournament in South Africa.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: MS Dhoni Retires From the IPL After 19 Years, Will Mentor CSK in 2027
articles.excerpt: Chennai Super Kings confirmed the end of Dhoni's playing career hours before the retention deadline. The five-title captain stays on as Team Mentor from IPL 2027.
articles.image_caption: MS Dhoni, in his Chennai Super Kings No. 7 jersey and wicketkeeping gloves, walks off during an IPL match. CSK announced on November 17, 2026 that Dhoni has retired as a player and will serve as the team's mentor from IPL 2027.
articles.nri_angle: Dhoni's retirement closes the playing career of the cricketer most diaspora fans grew up watching; his mentor role keeps him in the IPL dugout for 2027, when CSK will tour global fan attention without him on the field.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: West Indies Set to Host Two India T20Is in the US or Canada in 2027
articles.excerpt: Two matches at one North American venue — Washington DC and Toronto are the frontrunners — are planned inside a July 2027 all-format tour, as Cricket West Indies pushes into the diaspora market.
articles.nri_angle: Two India T20Is on US or Canadian soil would put the Indian team within reach of the large Indian and Caribbean diaspora crowds in cities like Toronto and Washington DC.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Patidar's 135 Off 48 and Suryakumar's 82 Off 29 Light Up SMAT
articles.excerpt: Madhya Pradesh posted a tournament-record 250 for 6 to rout Assam, while Mumbai chased 198 in 15.4 overs against Gujarat in Monday's Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy action.
articles.nri_angle: Domestic T20 form is the selection pathway diaspora fans follow between internationals, and both innings bear directly on India's next T20I squad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jay Shah Reappointed Unopposed as ICC Chair for Second Term
articles.excerpt: The ICC Board confirmed Shah's second term at its Bali meetings. He now leads the game through the 2027 World Cup in Southern Africa and cricket's Olympic return at Los Angeles 2028.
articles.nri_angle: Shah's second term puts an Indian administrator in charge as cricket stages its Olympic return at Los Angeles 2028, the diaspora's home market in the United States.

articles.title: 'We Never Stopped Believing': Raichandani on India's Last-Ball U19 Asia Cup Final Win
articles.excerpt: India's U19 captain, who made 80 in the chase of 338, said the plan was always to take the final deep - and that the dressing room trusted a batting order that ran almost 11 deep.
articles.nri_angle: The captain's account closes out a final diaspora fans followed ball by ball - a record ninth U19 Asia Cup title, won off the last delivery against Pakistan.

articles.title: India Lands 2029 Champions Trophy and 2031 World Cup in ICC Calendar to 2035
articles.excerpt: The ICC Board, meeting in Bali, fixed windows for its major men's events through 2035: India hosts the Champions Trophy in October 2029 and shares the 2031 World Cup with Bangladesh.
articles.image_caption: Fans arriving at Edgbaston Cricket Ground for an ICC Champions Trophy match between England and Australia. India will host the 2029 Champions Trophy and co-host the 2031 ODI World Cup under the ICC calendar to 2035.
articles.nri_angle: Fans in the US, UK and the Gulf get fixed windows years ahead for India's two home tournaments: the 2029 Champions Trophy and the 2031 World Cup co-hosted with Bangladesh.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Who Is Harmanpreet Kaur? The Moga Batter Who Captained India to Its First Women's World Cup — and Just Became the First Female Cricketer Honoured With a Wax Statue
articles.excerpt: Born in Moga, Punjab, Harmanpreet Kaur debuted for India at 20, announced herself with 171 not out in a World Cup semi-final, captained India in 211 internationals to its first Women's World Cup in 2025 — then stepped down in October 2026 and, weeks later, unveiled a wax statue in Jaipur organisers call the world's first of a female cricketer.
articles.image_caption: Harmanpreet Kaur poses alongside her wax statue at its unveiling in Jaipur on November 13, 2026. Organisers describe the figure, bound for the Historica museum at Nahargarh Fort, as the world's first wax statue of a female cricketer.
articles.nri_angle: The Moga-born all-rounder who became the first Indian woman signed by an overseas franchise — playing in front of diaspora crowds in Australia's Big Bash and England's Hundred — captained India to its first Women's World Cup in 2025 and remains the face diaspora fans associate with the women's game's rise.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Seal ODI Series 3-1 in New Zealand, Hold No. 1 Ranking
articles.excerpt: Defending just 209 at Bay Oval, India's pace attack triggered a New Zealand collapse from 64 for 1 to 119 for 6, sealing a 22-run win and a nine-point lead at the top of the ICC ODI rankings.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora fans, India enter the new year as the world's top-ranked ODI side, with a two-Test series against New Zealand starting November 19 next on the calendar.

articles.title: India Beat Pakistan by One Wicket in Last-Ball U19 Asia Cup Final
articles.excerpt: Chasing 338 at Al Amerat, India recovered from 252 for eight to finish on 339 for nine off the final ball — Mohit Ulva unbeaten on 49 — and claim a record ninth U19 Asia Cup title.
articles.nri_angle: A last-ball India-Pakistan final is the fixture diaspora fans follow most closely at age-group level, and this one delivered a record ninth continental title for India.

articles.title: KPMG Opens Bengaluru Sports Tech Hub as It Eyes a $40 Billion Indian Sports Industry by 2030
articles.excerpt: The hub, launched November 13, will build AI and data products for athlete performance, talent identification and fan engagement. KPMG values India's sports industry at about $21 billion today.
articles.nri_angle: The hub's fan-engagement and streaming work is aimed at an audience that includes the diaspora following Indian leagues from abroad.

articles.title: India Face Pakistan in U19 Asia Cup Final, Chasing a Record Ninth Title
articles.excerpt: Raichandani's India meet unbeaten defending champions Pakistan in Al Amerat on Saturday at 10:30 a.m. IST — 9 p.m. Friday on the US West Coast — after Pakistan won their group meeting by three wickets.
articles.nri_angle: The final starts at 10:30 a.m. IST on Saturday, which is 9:00 p.m. PT on Friday and midnight ET — a prime-time watch for diaspora fans in North America.

articles.title: Ares Management Reportedly in Talks for Minority Stake in Kolkata Knight Riders
articles.excerpt: Moneycontrol reporting says the US asset manager is in advanced discussions over about 20% of the IPL franchise from the Mehta Group, at a valuation of over $1.8 billion — with no final agreement reached.
articles.image_caption: The Eden Gardens stadium just before the beginning of the Indian Premier League match between the Kolkata Knight Riders and the Chennai Super Kings, on the 18th of May, 2008. US alternative asset manager Ares Management is reportedly in talks to acquire a minority stake in Kolkata Knight Riders, according to Moneycontrol reporting cited in fresh reports this week — no final agreement has been reached.
articles.image_credit: Photo: Partha Bhaumik via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)
articles.nri_angle: KKR's owner group also runs the Los Angeles Knight Riders in Major League Cricket, so a US institutional buyer for the IPL franchise would deepen the Knight Riders brand's American footprint.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gambhir 'Concerned' by India's Batting Collapses After 244-Run Rout in New Zealand
articles.excerpt: India folded for 89 chasing 334 at Mount Maunganui, their second-heaviest ODI defeat. The head coach said the repeat collapses — not one bad innings — are the problem, in conditions he called the closest thing to next year's World Cup.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora fans watching the New Zealand tour are seeing the exact conditions India will face at the 2027 World Cup in Southern Africa — which is why Gambhir is treating a bilateral collapse as a warning, not a blip.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Harmanpreet Kaur Unveils Wax Statue in Jaipur, Says 171 Knock Changed Women's Cricket
articles.excerpt: The former India captain's figure will stand permanently beside Tendulkar and Dhoni at Nahargarh Fort. At the unveiling she credited her 171-run innings with changing perceptions, and told young women cricketers to bat like Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora fans who watched the 171 and the World Cup run from abroad, the Jaipur statue marks women's cricket's arrival in the same hall of fame long reserved for Tendulkar, Dhoni and Kohli.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.excerpt: An early Bijoy Varghese own goal, a Jesse Randall brace, and second-half goals from Chris Wood and Lachlan Bayliss gave New Zealand a 5-0 win in the opening match of India's New Zealand tour; the sides meet again in Christchurch on Sunday.
articles.image_caption: India's starting eleven pose for a team photograph before the friendly at Go Media Stadium in Auckland. New Zealand won the match 5-0, with Jesse Randall scoring twice.
articles.nri_angle: India's first match in New Zealand drew the diaspora's football fans in Auckland; the second friendly in Christchurch on Sunday, November 15 is the next chance to watch the Blue Tigers in person or on the morning IST broadcast.

articles.title: Unbeaten 249-Run Stand Puts Sri Lanka Within 30 Runs of Pakistan in Rawalpindi
articles.excerpt: Dhananjaya de Silva (167 not out) and captain Kusal Mendis (117 not out) batted through Day 3 of the first Test, taking Sri Lanka to 404 for 4 against Pakistan's 434 for 9 declared, with Pakistan taking only one wicket all day.
articles.nri_angle: A record Rawalpindi fifth-wicket stand in a Pakistan-Sri Lanka Test — the kind of subcontinental contest South Asian diaspora fans follow closely.

articles.title: Rohit Sharma Thanks Bharat Army for 'Rock Solid' Support Ahead of Fourth ODI
articles.excerpt: In a video message shared by the Bharat Army, Rohit signed a 'Thank You Bharat Army' jersey as India, leading New Zealand 2-0, prepare for the fourth ODI at Bay Oval, Mount Maunganui, on Friday.
articles.nri_angle: The Bharat Army is the diaspora's travelling fan community; Rohit's message was aimed at supporters who follow India across overseas tours.

articles.title: Bengaluru Police Recover Somaya's Stolen 1980 Olympic Gold and Seven Other Medals
articles.excerpt: Two men have been arrested and all eight international medals stolen from the former India hockey captain's home have been recovered, along with valuables worth about Rs 3.5 lakh.
articles.nri_angle: Somaya's 1980 Moscow gold is part of the sporting history diaspora hockey fans grew up on; its recovery closes a theft that reached from a Bengaluru home to India's last Olympic hockey title.

articles.title: Hardik Pandya Traded to Punjab Kings as Arshdeep Singh Joins Mumbai Indians
articles.excerpt: The IPL formally announced on Wednesday that Mumbai Indians captain Hardik Pandya will move to Punjab Kings at a revised fee of Rs 18 crore, with Arshdeep Singh joining Mumbai at his existing Rs 18 crore fee, ahead of the November 17 retention deadline.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora IPL fans get the retention deadline of November 17 and the December 16 Goa mini-auction as the next dates that will reshape both squads.

articles.excerpt: Overlooked for the senior tour of South Africa, off-spinning all-rounder Shreyanka Patil has been named in all three India A squads for the home series against England A starting November 30 in Pune, with Kashvee Gautam also returning from knee surgery.
articles.image_caption: Shreyanka Patil bowls for India in a T20 international. She has been named in all three India A squads for the England A series starting November 30.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora fans following Indian women's cricket get the full England A schedule, with the Pune T20s from November 30 and the Wankhede one-dayers on December 8, 11 and 14.
